# Adjudication Task — Chapter 903

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃903화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|아무리 고민해도 답이 나오지 않는 수수께끼가 있다면, 해결하는 방법은 하나뿐이다.
  6|
  7|모든 것을 거꾸로 뒤집는 것.
  8|
  9|지금까지 파악한 정황, 단서를 모두 잊고 처음부터 시작하는 것만이 마지막 대책이다.
 10|
 11|언제 흘렸는지 모를 귀중품을 찾기 위해 왔던 길을 되돌아가는 것처럼, 나 역시 시작점에서부터 크고 작은 하나하나를 되짚었다.
 12|
 13|그리고 마침내, 하나의 가설에 도달할 수 있었다.
 14|
 15|“황제는, 상산왕이 위기에 빠지는 걸 원치 않는다.”
 16|
 17|“……!”
 18|
 19|창공의 회색빛 눈동자에 일어난 미약한 파문.
 20|
 21|그것은 찰나라고 부를 만큼 짧은 순간 만에 나타났다가 사라졌으나, 그의 작은 움직임 하나하나에 촉각을 곤두세우고 있던 내 이목을 피할 수는 없었다.
 22|
 23|‘사실이었어.’
 24|
 25|머릿속을 강타한 깨달음과 함께 찌릿한 전류가 등줄기를 타고 흐른다.
 26|
 27|아직도 사그라지지 않은 사람들의 거대한 함성 속에서, 나를 물끄러미 바라보던 창공이 불현듯 입을 열었다.
 28|
 29|“언제부터였나?”
 30|
 31|다른 누군가였다면 이해하지 못했을, 맥락 없는 물음.
 32|
 33|그러나 나는 즉각 그 말이 가리키는 의미를 깨달았다.
 34|
 35|도대체 언제부터 자신들을 의심하기 시작했냐는 그 질문을.
 36|
 37|“소교.”
 38|
 39|그래, 정확히 그때부터였다.
 40|
 41|도저히 실패할 수 없던 유리한 상황에서 날 놔준 그 날.
 42|
 43|그 어떤 정황과 단서로도 소교가 보인 기이한 행동은 완전히 이해할 수 없었다.
 44|
 45|마치 목에 걸린 생선 가시처럼.
 46|
 47|“소교라…….”
 48|
 49|내 짤막한 대답에 창공이 작게 고개를 끄덕였다.
 50|
 51|“그래, 그랬겠지. 이 대계의 유일한 허점이었으니까. 이럴 줄 알았다면 저 정체 모를 여자를 진작 제거해야 했다. 설령 황제와 전면전을 치르는 한이 있더라도.”
 52|
 53|뭐?
 54|
 55|반사적으로 튀어나오려는 목소리를 애써 삼켰지만, 찰나의 동요까지는 숨기지 못했다.
 56|
 57|‘창공조차도 소교의 정체를 모른다고?’
 58|
 59|순간 나도 모르게 얼굴에 떠오른 당혹감을 읽어 낸 창공이 낮은 웃음을 흘렸다.
 60|
 61|“보아하니 자네도 모르는 모양이군. 저 여자가 누구인지. 심지어 아군인지 적군인지조차.”
 62|
 63|“……!”
 64|
 65|“희한하군. 참으로 희한해. 조금 전까지는 무림맹의 끄나풀이 아닐까 의심했는데…… 이제는 도무지 모르겠군. 황실이 비밀리에 키워 낸 고수라고 해도 노부의 이목을 피할 수 없었을 터인데.”
 66|
 67|이번만큼은 내가 처한 이 모든 상황을 떠나 창공이 느끼는 의문에 공감할 수밖에 없었다.
 68|
 69|‘그렇다면 소교는, 저 여자는 누구지?’
 70|
 71|무림맹에 속한 인물이었다면 이런 상황이 오기 전에 내게 모든 진실을 알려 주었을 테고, 암천이나 황실의 고수라면 창공이 모를 리 없다.
 72|
 73|하지만 소교는 달랐다.
 74|
 75|지금까지 확인된 바에 의하면 그녀는 제삼의 인물이었다.
 76|
 77|그 어디에도 소속되지 않은.
 78|
 79|‘도대체.’
 80|
 81|소교는 누구일까. 지금쯤 어떤 표정으로, 무슨 생각으로 우리를 바라보고 있을까.
 82|
 83|그리고…….
 84|
 85|‘적군일까. 아군일까.’
 86|
 87|나는 저 멀리, 높게 솟은 계단 위에 서 있을 소교를 향해 고개를 돌리고 싶은 충동을 애써 억눌렀다.
 88|
 89|창공과 나 사이의 거리는 불과 몇 걸음. 이런 상황에서 잠깐이라도 시선을 돌리는 것은 자살행위나 다름없다.
 90|
 91|물론, 이렇게 배짱을 부리는 것도 창공이 당장 나를 죽일 수 없다는 확신이 있었기 때문이었지만.
 92|
 93|“눈빛이 좋군. 투기(鬪氣)가 흘러넘쳐. 하지만 무슨 연유로 그분께서 자네에게 관심을 보이시는 걸까.”
 94|
 95|그분.
 96|
 97|이곳에 없는 누군가를 지칭하는 창공의 목소리에서, 숨길 수 없는 두려움과 경애를 느낀 것은 단순한 착각이 아닐 것이다.
 98|
 99|혈주도, 서천마군도, 그리고 남천마후도 그러했으니까.
100|
101|저들 암천(暗天)은, 천주(天主)라는 하늘이 있기에 존재하는 집단이었으니까.
102|
103|“한번 말해 보게. 당사자라면 그분께서 이토록 자네를 찾는 연유를 알 수도 있겠지. 이토록 어린 나이에 전무후무한 성취를 보여 주어서? 아니면 그분만이 알아볼 수 있는 또 다른 진가 때문에?”
104|
105|마치 죽은 이의 그것과 같은 회색빛 눈동자가 흐릿하게 빛났다.
106|
107|내가 지금껏 느껴 보지 못한, 은밀하면서도 무시무시한 한기와 함께.
108|
109|스아아아.
110|
111|감히 장담컨대, 남만에서 나를 궁지에 몰아넣었던 대설귀(大雪鬼)의 음한지기(陰寒之氣)조차도 이 정도는 아니었다.
112|
113|‘아니, 음한지기와는 달라.’
114|
115|보다 원초적이고 순수한 무언가.
116|
117|들어 본 적도, 겪어 본 적도 없는 또 다른 힘.
118|
119|그러나 나는 본능적인 두려움을 이겨 냈다. 뼛속까지 스며드는 서늘한 기운을 견디며 대답했다.
120|
121|“그걸 왜 나한테 묻고 지랄이야. 불알도 없는 새끼가.”
122|
123|“……!”
124|
125|크게 뜨인 눈동자로 나를 바라보던 창공이 희미하게 웃었다.
126|
127|“그래, 당연히 모르겠지. 어찌 자네 따위가 감히 그분의 뜻을 헤아릴 수 있…….”
128|
129|“응. 아무리 뜻을 헤아려도 찾아볼 수 없는 니 불알.”
130|
131|“단어 선택에 신중을 기하는 것이 좋을 걸세. 제아무리 노부가 그분께 하해와 같은 은혜를 입었다고는 해도…….”
132|
133|“응. 하해를 뒤져도 찾을 수 없는 니 고환.”
134|
135|“…….”
136|
137|“단어 선택에 신중을 기했는데, 무슨 문제라도?”
138|
139|조금 전의 희미한 미소는 이미 사라진 지 오래.
140|
141|아직도 그치지 않은 사람들의 환호성 속에서, 굳게 닫혀 있던 창공의 창백한 입술이 열렸다.
142|
143|“어떤가. 혓바닥을 뽑는 정도라면, 그분께서도 충분히 이해해주실 거라 생각하지 않나?”
144|
145|“맞아. 천주라면 그럴 수도 있겠지. 안 그래도 불알 없는 놈이라 수하 중에서도 유독 신경 쓰이는 아픈 불알…… 아니, 아픈 손가락일 테니까.”
146|
147|고개를 끄덕여 수긍한 내가 말을 이었다.
148|
149|창공의 어깨너머를 가리키며.
150|
151|“하지만 저 양반은 이해 안 해 줄걸.”
152|
153|그 순간.
154|
155|느려진 시간 속에서, 모든 것이 동시에 이루어졌다.
156|
157|무심코 등 뒤를 향해 고개를 돌리는 창공. 그런 창공을 향해 화염이 실린 일권(一拳)을 뻗는 나.
158|
159|그리고 마치 홀로 시간을 역행하듯, 섬광 같은 속도로 쏘아진 내 주먹이 누군가의 육신에 닿기도 전에 앞질러 가로막은 단단한 손바닥.
160|
161|콰아앙!
162|
163|하늘이 쪼개지는 듯한 굉음이 느려졌던 시간을 되돌린다. 동시에 강대한 여파가 대연회장을 흔들었다.
164|
165|콰득, 드드드득!
166|
167|지진이라도 난 것처럼 흔들리는 대지.
168|
169|사방에서 터져 나오는 비명과 고함.
170|
171|순식간에 극심한 혼란에 빠진 그 공간 속에서, 나를 응시하는 한 쌍의 새하얀 안광(眼光)이 있었다.
172|
173|“고작, 이 정도였나?”
174|
175|우둑.
176|
177|담담한 목소리와는 달리 거대한 힘이 내 주먹을 옥죄인다.
178|
179|정체를 알 수 없는 얼음 같은 기운이 그 안에 깃든 화염을 억누르고 꺼트렸다.
180|
181|“이런 얕은 수작을 부리다니, 실망이군.”
182|
183|으득. 으드득.
184|
185|붙잡힌 주먹으로부터 끔찍한 고통이 전해진다.
186|
187|아마도 인간의 경지를 벗어난 근골이 아니었다면 진작 가루처럼 으스러지고도 남았을 상황.
188|
189|하지만 이 정도 고통은 이미 질릴 만큼 겪어 봤고, 이 정도 기습으로 놈을 쓰러트릴 수 있다는 생각은 처음부터 하지도 않았다.
190|
191|그저, 이 상황을 알릴 수 있는 신호탄이 필요했을 뿐이었다.
192|
193|“단순히 얕은 수작이라고 생각했다면 조금 섭섭한데.”
194|
195|“뭐라?”
196|
197|“마법이라고 들어 봤는지 모르겠는데, 이참에 직접 보여 줄 테니까 꼭 한 번 봐봐.”
198|
199|“그게 무슨…….”
200|
201|창공이 눈살을 찌푸린 그 순간.
202|
203|콰아아앙!
204|
205|어둠마저 집어삼키는 눈부신 화염과 함께, 높게 솟은 성벽처럼 대연회장을 둘러싼 암벽들이 터져나갔다.
206|
207|그리고 조금 전 잠시나마 창공의 시선이 향했던 그곳으로, 한 인영이 성큼성큼 걸어 나왔다.
208|
209|“노부가 처음이자 마지막으로 충고하건대.”
210|
211|아무리 봐도 불가(佛家)와는 한참 동떨어진, 화염이 일렁이는 두 눈으로 좌중을 쓸어본 땡중이 말을 이었다.
212|
213|“뼈와 살이 녹아내리고 싶은 놈만 앞으로 나서거라.”
214|
215|“……!”
216|
217|불청객의 정체를 알아차린 창공의 눈빛이 깊게 가라앉았고, 나는 웃으며 입을 열었다.
218|
219|“아씨오, 화왕.”
220|
221|그리고 동시에, 아직 자유로운 한 손을 뻗었다.
222|
223|순간 멈칫한 놈의 가슴을 향해.
224|
225|구 성에 이른 화염신장(火焰神掌)을.
226|
227|꽈아아아앙!
228|
229|
230|
231|* * *
232|
233|
234|
235|“어?”
236|
237|문득 걸음을 멈춘 청년이 고개를 돌렸다.
238|
239|미간을 좁힌 채 자신이 왔던 길을 빤히 응시하는 그의 모습에, 한발 앞서가던 거한이 물었다.
240|
241|“혁무. 왜 그러나?”
242|
243|“아니, 그냥…….”
244|
245|말꼬리를 흐린 혁무진은 입맛을 다셨다.
246|
247|“그냥, 무슨 소리가 들린 것 같아서.”
248|
249|그 말을 들은 거한, 태산이 눈썹을 치켜세웠다.
250|
251|“소리? 그렇다면 적인가?”
252|
253|“모르겠는데. 그냥 내가 착각했던 건가?”
254|
255|“그럼 아니다. 혁무가 들었다는 그 소리. 태산이는 못 들었다.”
256|
257|“하지만 분명히 뭔가 들은 것 같았다니까.”
258|
259|“혁무. 무공 낮다. 태산이가 마음만 먹으면 잘 다진 오향장육으로 만들 수 있다.”
260|
261|“……아니, 그런데 이 새끼가 진짜. 지금 나 무시하냐?”
262|
263|“으음. 솔직히 약간.”
264|
265|“…….”
266|
267|“혁무. 우리 멈추면 안 된다. 이제 가야 한다. 모두들 기다린다.”
268|
269|순간 울컥했던 마음을 가라앉힌 혁무진은 한숨을 푹 내쉬었다.
270|
271|“그래, 간다. 가.”
272|
273|하지만 대답과는 달리 걸음은 전처럼 가볍게 나아가지 않았다.
274|
275|자신이 이미 지나쳐 온 저 길이, 지금 이 순간에도 조금씩 멀어지고 있는 황도(皇都)의 성벽이 자꾸만 눈앞에 아른거렸다.
276|
277|‘젠장. 이제는 하다 하다 환청까지 들리나?’
278|
279|조금 울컥하긴 했지만, 아무 소리도 안 났다는 태산의 대답이 사실일 가능성이 높았다.
280|
281|한 수 위의 절정고수인 그가 아니라면 아닌 거니까.
282|
283|정말 뭔가를 들었다고는 해도 벌레나 짐승이 움직이는 미세한 소음 정도였을 것이다.
284|
285|‘그런데 왜 이러는 거지?’
286|
287|혁무진은 미간을 더욱 좁히며 자신의 가슴을 두드렸다.
288|
289|안 그랬던 심장이 자꾸만 쿵쿵 뛴다. 마치 보이지 않는 손이 힘껏 쥐어짜고 있는 것처럼.
290|
291|‘기분이 이상해.’
292|
293|알 수 없는 불안감과 동시에, 문득 몇 시진 전 헤어졌던 한 사람의 얼굴이 눈앞을 스쳤다.
294|
295|
296|
297|‘임무 하나만 하자.’
298|
299|
300|
301|떠나기 직전 들었던 마지막 목소리가 귓가에 맴돌았다.
302|
303|
304|

“Why the hell are you asking me, you ball-less bastard?”

[P58]
“…!”

[P59]

[P60]
“Yes, of course you wouldn’t know. How could someone like you presume to fathom that person’s intentions—”

[P61]
“Yeah. No matter how hard I try to fathom them, I still can’t find your balls.”

[P62]
“Choose your words carefully. No matter how generously that person has blessed me…”

[P63]
“Yeah. I could search the whole ocean of his generosity and still not find your testicles.”

[P64]
“…”

[P65]
“I chose my words carefully. What’s the problem?”

[P66]

[P67]
“What do you think? Surely that person would understand if I merely pulled out your tongue.”

[P68]
“Sure. The Lord of Heaven might. Being the one follower without balls must make you a particularly sore ball—no, a sore finger.”

[P69]

[P70]
“But that guy won’t understand.”

[P71]
In that instant, everything happened at once.

[P72]
Cang Gong turned his head to look behind him. I drove a flame-wreathed fist at him.

[P73]
And as though it alone were moving backward through time, a solid palm shot out at blinding speed and stopped my fist before it could touch anyone.

[P74]
*BOOM!*

[P75]
A roar like the sky splitting open brought time rushing back to normal. At the same instant, a powerful shock wave shook the grand banquet hall.

[P76]
*Crack! Rrrrmm!*

[P77]
The ground shuddered as though an earthquake had struck.

[P78]
Screams and shouts erupted on all sides.

[P79]
Amid the sudden chaos, a pair of gleaming white eyes fixed on me.

[P80]
“Was that all?”

[P81]
*Crack.*

[P82]
His voice was calm. The immense force crushing my fist was anything but.

[P83]
An unknown, ice-cold energy filled his palm, suppressing the flames in mine and snuffing them out.

[P84]
“Such a shallow trick. I’m disappointed.”

[P85]
*Crunch. Crunch.*

[P86]
Agonizing pain shot through my captured fist.

[P87]
If my muscles and bones hadn’t surpassed the limits of an ordinary human, they would already have been ground to dust.

[P88]
But I’d endured this much pain more times than I cared to count. And I’d never expected that surprise attack to bring him down.

[P89]
I’d only needed a signal flare to let everyone know what was happening.

[P90]
“I’m a little hurt that you think it was just a shallow trick.”

[P91]
“What?”

[P92]
“I don’t know if you’ve heard of magic, but I’m about to show you some. Watch closely.”

[P93]
“What are you—”

[P94]
Cang Gong frowned.

[P95]
*BOOOOM!*

[P96]
Blinding flames swallowed the darkness, and the rock walls that ringed the grand banquet hall like towering ramparts burst apart.

[P97]
From the place Cang Gong had glanced toward moments earlier, a figure strode out.

[P98]
“I’ll give you my first and last warning.”

[P99]
The damn monk swept his flame-filled eyes over everyone in the hall. There was nothing Buddhist about that gaze.

[P100]
“Only step forward if you want your flesh and bones to melt.”

[P101]
“…!”

[P102]
Recognition darkened Cang Gong’s eyes. I smiled.

[P103]
“Accio, Fire King.”

[P104]
At the same time, I thrust out my still-free hand toward his chest. He faltered for an instant.

[P105]
The Flame Divine Palm, at nine-tenths mastery.

[P106]
*BOOOOM!*

[P107]
* * *

[P108]
“Huh?”

[P109]
The young man stopped abruptly and looked back.

[P110]
Seeing him stare down the road they’d traveled, his brow furrowed, the burly man ahead of him asked, “Hyukmu. What’s wrong?”

[P111]
“No, it’s just…”

[P112]
Hyuk Mujin trailed off and smacked his lips.

[P113]
“I thought I heard something.”

[P114]
Taishan raised an eyebrow. “A sound? An enemy?”

[P115]
“I don’t know. Maybe I imagined it.”

[P116]
“Then no. That sound Hyukmu heard—Taishan didn’t hear it.”

[P117]
“But I’m telling you, I’m sure I heard something.”

[P118]
“Hyukmu. Your martial arts are weak. Taishan could turn you into finely minced five-spice pork if he wanted.”

[P119]
“…Hey, what the hell? Are you looking down on me?”

[P120]
“Mm. Honestly, a little.”

[P121]
“…”

[P122]
“Hyukmu. We can’t stop. We have to go. Everyone’s waiting.”

[P123]
Hyuk Mujin swallowed his flare of anger and let out a long sigh.

[P124]
“Yeah, I’m coming. I’m coming.”

[P125]
But despite his answer, his steps didn’t come as easily as before.

[P126]
The road behind him and the walls of the Imperial Capital, growing more distant by the moment, kept appearing before his eyes.

[P127]
*Damn it. Am I hearing things now?*

[P128]
Annoying as it was, Taishan was probably right that there hadn’t been a sound. If a Peak master a step above him hadn’t heard it, then there was nothing to hear.

[P129]
Even if Mujin *had* heard something, it must have been the faint noise of an insect or an animal moving.

[P130]
*Then why do I feel like this?*

[P131]
Hyuk Mujin frowned harder and thumped his chest.

[P132]
His heart kept pounding when it hadn’t before, as though an invisible hand were squeezing it tight.

[P133]
*Something feels wrong.*

[P134]
Along with that inexplicable unease came the face of someone he’d parted from a few shichen ago.

[P135]
*Just one mission.*

[P136]
The last voice he’d heard before leaving still echoed in his ears.

[P137]
*Oh, one more thing.*

[P138]
*Yes?*

[P139]
*Be careful. You and everyone else.*

[P140]
Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.

[P141]
Hyuk Mujin had answered the warning with a grin. Then he and the rest of the Fire Dragon Pavilion had left the Imperial Capital, bound for the border between Jiangsu and Zhejiang Provinces.

[P142]
For the very place written on the note Jin Taekyung had given him.

[P143]
*The mission’s going fine… so what’s wrong with me?*

[P144]
Everything was going smoothly, yet his chest felt unbearably tight.

[P145]
The Captain—Jin Taekyung—had acted so strangely that the memory pricked at him like a fishbone caught in his throat.

[P146]
Taekyung usually laughed with him over nothing, hit him for getting cheeky, and cursed him without holding back. Today, Mujin had seen none of that.

[P147]
“Hyukmu!”

[P148]
“…Ah.”

[P149]
Snapping out of his thoughts, Hyuk Mujin realized he’d stopped walking again.

[P150]
Then he saw his companions waiting a short distance ahead, and his heart sank.

[P151]
Grave eyes. Troubled faces.

[P152]
Everyone except Taishan was looking at him the same way.

[P153]
“Everyone…”

[P154]
Hyuk Mujin barely swallowed a groan. At last, he thought he understood the unease that had been squeezing his chest.

[P155]
“Did you all know?”

[P156]
Namho answered his halting question in a heavy voice.

[P157]
“Yes. More or less.”

[P158]
“The Captain told you?”

[P159]
“No. Senior Jeok gave us a warning beforehand. He knew what choice his Disciple would make.”

[P160]
“Then why was I the only one—”

[P161]
“If he’d told you to leave because you’d be a burden, would you have obeyed without a fuss?”

[P162]
“…!”

[P163]
“I don’t like this either. None of us do.”

[P164]
For a moment, Hyuk Mujin had nothing to say.

[P165]
He understood perfectly well how they felt about being burdens instead of help. He understood why Jin Taekyung had lied to send him away.

[P166]
And they were right.

[P167]
But… but…

[P168]
*Still, it shouldn’t have been like this.*

[P169]
Hyuk Mujin bit his lip until it bled and turned his head. Then he forgot everything else and muttered in a daze.

[P170]
“Huh…?”

[P171]
Far away, countless figures moved through the darkness, shaking the forest as they passed.

[P172]
Too many to count, yet he couldn’t sense a single presence among them.

[P173]
*What are those?*

[P174]
The same question arose in everyone’s mind. So did a fear none of them could explain.

[P175]
This time, instinct rather than reason moved Hyuk Mujin.

[P176]
No—it moved them all.

[P177]
*Whoosh!*

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
